extractor.note: Read every paragraph carrying transcend- (outside transcendental), immanen-, surpass, overstep or going beyond, in file order. The 1925 stratum is set only on the numbered lecture sections; the Beilagen and the separately numbered later pieces carry none.

coverage_note: Term-led pass over the whole file (lines 1-1703): every paragraph containing the transcendence family, including bare transcendent and immanent, was read; paragraphs without such a word were not read.

units.claim: Explanatory psychology, as reported in Dilthey's critique, proceeds like physics by hypothetical inferences that transcend experiencing intuition.
units.quote: It proceeds, like physics, hypothetically and constructively, by means of inferences that transcend experiencing intuition.

units.claim: The unity of the world is not a posit added to experience but an immanent character of the experiential stream.
units.quote: The point is: the world's unity is not a posit added to experience but an immanent character of the experiential stream itself.

units.claim: Limiting itself to the sphere of perception, the lecture brings to evidence the fundamental distinction between immanence and transcendence documented in pure subjectivity itself.
units.quote: namely, the fundamental distinction between immanence and transcendence documented in pure subjectivity itself

units.claim: Inner perception is perception of the immanent and outer perception is perception of the transcendent.
units.quote: Now we can also say: inner perception is perception of the immanent; outer perception is perception of the transcendent.

units.claim: What is taken from the immanent time-sphere of the experience-stream as an immanent time-object or its reell parts and moments is immanent.
units.quote: Everything that we take from this immanent time-sphere as singly-immanent time-object — as one such time-object's reell parts or moments — is immanent.

units.claim: The transcendent object is the irreal pole of perception, belonging reell to no lived-experience but meant in all of them as the one they present.
units.quote: The transcendent object is the irreal pole of perception — it does not belong reell to any lived-experience, but is inseparably meant-in-them as the one that they all present.

units.claim: The object transcends the reell content of the experience-stream, and this concept of the transcendent as object conscious in immanence carries difficulties and ambiguities.
units.quote: Yet this concept of the transcendent — as the object conscious in immanence — carries with it many great difficulties and shimmering ambiguities, and demands further consideration.

units.claim: The ideal pole, the object as transcendent, is not a rigid piece common to all the intentional experiences in which it dwells.
units.quote: The ideal-pole (the object as transcendent) is not something like a rigid piece common to all the intentional experiences in which it ideally dwells.

units.claim: The object is transcendent in another sense than polar irreality: as perceptually given in belief, it cannot be completed by any synthetically extended perception into adequate givenness.
units.quote: It itself is transcendent to perception in yet another sense than that of the polar irreality — namely in that of a perceptually-given

units.claim: The intentional object is transcendent to the lived-experience, not reell in it, yet immanent in the strict sense of belonging inseparably to it as noematic correlate.
units.quote: The intentional object is transcendent to the lived-experience (it is not reell in it) but immanent in the strict sense of belonging inseparably to the lived-experience as its noematic correlate.

units.claim: With the distinctions of immanence and transcendence in hand, the reduction is formulated as the change of attitude that unveils the purely immanent domain of consciousness and its correlates.
units.quote: The reduction is a change of attitude whereby the natural positing of the world is bracketed and what remains is the purely immanent domain of consciousness and its correlates.

units.claim: In the phenomenological attitude the outer object is thematic only as the transcendent meaning of the perception, and the transcendent intentionality contained in the subjective is co-thematic.
units.quote: and if subjective contains in itself transcendent intentionality as its meaning, then that — and the analysis of this meaning as such — is co-thematic

units.claim: That a perception perceives a transcendent and posits it as being is a type of truth that, grasped phenomenologically, contains no meaning about the transcendent world simpliciter.
units.quote: that a perception perceives a transcendent and that it thereby in its belief-certainty posits its object as being (and posits with a transcendent sense of this or that structure) — this is a type of truths that, phenomenologically purely grasped, contains in itself not the slightest meaning about the transcendent world simpliciter

units.claim: The subjective consciousness-life in pure immanence is the site of all sense-giving and being-positing, which calls for a pure self-clarification of the knower.
units.quote: So the subjective consciousness-life in pure immanence is the site of all sense-giving and being-positing, being-corroborating.

units.claim: Empirical psychology did not seek the psychic as a transcendent, indirectly determined object, which is the source of the need for a descriptive psychology.
units.quote: In the long-ruling empirical psychology, the psychic is not sought as a transcendent and indirectly theoretically determined — and this is the source of the need for a descriptive psychology.

absences.expected_because: The section continues the pole analysis of §34, where the object as transcendent was defined as the irreal pole of perception.
The reflective turn onto the perception of physical things is the starting point from which §§31-34 draw the distinction of immanent and transcendent perception.
